messages.content: Can you help me make the final flight call for the Upper Midwest loop? I have a Delta nonstop SLC to MSP Sunday Oct. 27, 2:05-5:42 p.m., which looks fine. Coming back Thursday after the 8:15 Eau Claire visit, I can either do the MSP nonstop at 4:50 p.m. or a cheaper Eau Claire one-stop around noon with a 38-minute connection. I don’t want to gamble the school visit just to save a little.

I’d book the MSP round trip. The Eau Claire option saves money, but it stacks the two things that are hardest to fix: a tight connection and a rental return at a smaller airport right after a school visit. With the MSP 4:50 nonstop, you can let the visit run a bit late, drive west without rushing, return the car at the same airport, and still avoid a huge dead stretch.
Visit should wrap by 9:30, maybe 10 if the counselor adds students. Is MSP still too much sitting around?

If you leave Eau Claire around 10:00, the drive plus gas and rental return puts you inside MSP around 12:15-12:45. For a 4:50 flight, that is a 3-ish hour cushion after security, not a full day. I would rather have that cushion than a 38-minute connection where a small delay strands you.
Okay, keep MSP. So rental is still MSP pickup and return?

Yes. Pick up Sunday evening at MSP and return Thursday early afternoon at MSP. No one-way return to price, no smaller-counter hours to worry about, and the Black River Falls-to-Eau Claire-to-MSP plan stays intact.
Good. Book economy. If seat selection is open, take window on both legs. What should I put in the receipt packet?

Booking note: buy the Sunday Oct. 27 SLC-MSP nonstop and the Thursday Oct. 31 4:50 p.m. MSP-SLC nonstop in economy, with window seats if available. Receipt packet: airfare receipt showing ticket number and full itinerary, any seat or bag fee receipts, rental confirmation showing MSP pickup and return, and later the final rental receipt with fuel or toll charges. Keep the school-visit schedule attached as the justification for the later MSP return flight.

messages.content: New thing: Denver admissions conference. It starts Tuesday Dec. 10 at noon and ends Thursday around 3. There’s a Wednesday evening reception near the convention center. I’m trying to decide whether to fly in Monday afternoon or Tuesday morning. Reimbursement cap is $190 before tax; the official hotel block is $229 and I can’t tell if breakfast is included.

Since the first required piece is Tuesday at noon, this is a reliability question. Monday afternoon is the safer arrival; Tuesday morning can work from SLC, but it leaves very little recovery time if weather, de-icing, or baggage slows you down. Two quick checks before I narrow it: do you need to be registered by a certain time Tuesday, and is a simple light-rail hop acceptable if it keeps the hotel under cap?
Registration by 11:15 would be ideal. Light rail is fine if it’s one easy ride, not a transfer with bags. I can leave after lunch Monday, but Tuesday would mean the very early flight.

Here’s how I’d weigh it: Monday afternoon arrival costs one extra hotel night but gives you a calm Tuesday morning and a normal check-in. Tuesday morning saves the night, but you’d need a nonstop landing by about 9:00 a.m. to leave room for airport transfer, bag drop, and registration. In December, I would not build this around a connection.
Can you shortlist hotels both ways? I need something I can show my director if she pushes back on the extra night.

Shortlist to compare: 1. Official block near the convention center: easiest for sessions and the reception, but $229 before tax and breakfast is unclear, so it needs reimbursement approval. 2. SpringHill Suites Denver Downtown/Auraria area: usually under or near cap, breakfast included, near a simple rail or ride option, but less convenient after the reception. 3. Element Denver Downtown East or similar edge-of-downtown option: walkable to the convention center, often closer to cap than the block, but dinner choices right outside are thinner.
SpringHill is showing $181 for Monday through Thursday, breakfast included. Element is $197, no clear breakfast, and the block is $229. Does that change the arrival answer?

Yes, it strengthens Monday. Three nights at SpringHill are still close to policy, and breakfast is solved. Two nights at the block cost nearly as much before you add breakfast, and it still needs an exception. If the director denies Monday, I’d still keep SpringHill for Tuesday and Wednesday because it is the cleanest reimbursement story.
What flight times would you search? Not booking yet.

For Plan A, search SLC-DEN nonstop Monday Dec. 9 departing roughly 1:00-4:00 p.m., arriving by early evening. That gives you dinner and a normal hotel check-in without burning the whole day. Return Thursday Dec. 12 after 5:00 p.m.; the conference ending around 3:00 makes anything earlier too tight once you include the airport ride and security.
And Plan B if I get told Tuesday only?

Plan B is a nonstop that lands at DEN by 9:00 a.m. Tuesday, ideally earlier, with no checked-bag dependency if you can avoid it. I’d avoid any Tuesday itinerary with a connection, because a small delay could make you miss registration or the opening session.
Can you give me the note I can send myself, including the hotel caveat?

Note for Denver: Recommended plan is Monday afternoon SLC-DEN nonstop, SpringHill/Auraria for Dec. 9-12 if the $181 breakfast-included rate is refundable and the rail or ride to the convention center is simple. Return Thursday after 5 p.m. If the extra hotel night is denied, use a very early Tuesday nonstop and book SpringHill for Dec. 10-12. Do not use the official block unless finance confirms the $229 rate is reimbursable above the $190 cap and whether breakfast is included or separately reimbursable. For the Wednesday reception, plan a rideshare back if the light-rail timing feels awkward.

messages.content: Denver rates shifted. For the two-night version, the block just sent a notice: only $239 king left, no breakfast listed. SpringHill/Auraria dropped to $166 with breakfast but it’s farther from the Wednesday reception. Element/Convention Center is $196, walkable, but there aren’t many easy food options around it. Can you rank these for booking?
I can, but one detail affects the order: are these all refundable, and are you now definitely booking only Tuesday and Wednesday nights?

Yes, Tuesday and Wednesday nights for now. SpringHill is refundable until 48 hours out. The block takes a one-night deposit but is refundable 72 hours out. Element becomes nonrefundable tomorrow evening. Cap is still $190 before tax, and the block email just says official conference rate.

My ranking: 1. SpringHill/Auraria at $166 with breakfast: best policy fit, easiest morning food, refundable, and the reception inconvenience is manageable for one evening. 2. Official block at $239 only if reimbursement gives written approval for the over-cap conference rate; otherwise it risks out-of-pocket cost and still leaves breakfast unresolved. 3. Element at $196: close enough to walk, but slightly over cap, nonrefundable soon, and weaker meal logistics, so it does not beat SpringHill.
Would you really not put the block first? It’s right there for the sessions.

If finance approves the $239 block rate in writing, I’d move it to first for convenience. Without that, the location benefit is not enough: you’d be above cap for both nights, may have to buy breakfast, and the deposit creates more cleanup if reimbursement is denied.
SpringHill says breakfast starts at 6:30. Reception ends around 8:30 p.m. The rail ride is 10 or 12 minutes, or I could rideshare. Too much hassle?

No, not for this agenda. Use light rail or a rideshare to the reception, then rideshare back after 8:30 if you do not want to wait. For the day sessions, leave 25-30 minutes from the hotel lobby so you are not cutting it close. Breakfast at 6:30 is early enough.
What exact reimbursement question should I send before I pay?

Ask this: Since the lower-priced conference-block rooms are sold out and the only remaining official block room is $239 before tax, will the university reimburse the actual official block rate above the $190 nightly cap, or will reimbursement be limited to $190 before tax? Also, please confirm whether the cap excludes taxes and required fees, and whether breakfast is reimbursable if it is not included.
If they say yes this afternoon, do I switch to the block?

Yes, if the approval is written and the room is still refundable, switch to the block for the shortest conference day logistics. If the answer is no or unclear, book SpringHill before its rate moves. I would skip Element unless SpringHill disappears or the rail plan becomes a problem.
